Stonebeck climbs as reopening markets carry gains forward

Rating: overweight

Stonebeck enters mid-March 2028 with the arithmetic of a cycle still finding its footing rather than losing it. Inflation at 2.4% sits close enough to target that the policy rate of 4.50% reads as a ceiling under pressure, not a floor giving way. Equities extend gains, and the ytd_return of +6.0% against a one_year_return of +15.0% describes compounding, not exhaustion. A drawdown of +0.0% confirms that this advance has not yet been tested by a real air pocket — which is a feature of a market still early in digesting policy support, not evidence of complacency.

Grimshaw Partners argues that fragilities are compounding beneath stable marks. We read the same surface differently: new issuance windows reopening is precisely the mechanism through which a constructive cycle clears its own throat. Credit markets do not reopen issuance into structures that are quietly rotting; they reopen when balance sheets have room to absorb fresh paper. The hy_spread_now_bps at 320bps is wide enough to compensate holders for real risk, yet narrow enough to signal that capital is willing to underwrite growth rather than flee it. The reported_vs_public_gap of -0.8% is modest — a rounding difference in measurement, not a structural warning light.
